title: Assistant Professor of Real Estate
description:
Work Authorization and Immigration Sponsorship

Wichita State University may be able to sponsor certain faculty
positions for employment-based immigration status where authorized
by the hiring department and university policy. Sponsorship
eligibility varies by faculty position and will be identified in
the individual job posting.

For faculty positions eligible for sponsorship, international
candidates generally must be eligible for sponsorship in a visa
classification compatible with the faculty position. For tenured
and tenure-track faculty appointments, visa classifications
incompatible with such appointments include F-1 Optional Practical
Training (OPT), J-1 Research Scholar, and J-1 Academic Training
statuses.

Department: Barton School of Business Department of Finance,
Real Estate, and Decision Sciences

Campus Location: Wichita, KS - WSU Main Campus

Hire Type: Full Time

Pay: Salary is set at $140,000/yr

Work Schedule: Based on course demands; work is performed
on-site and in person.

Export Compliance Requirement: No export control
requirement.

Job Story

Candidates will have an exciting opportunity to help shape the
future of real estate education and research at Wichita State
University. The position will play an important role in advancing
the Real Estate program, strengthening partnerships with the real
estate industry, and contributing to the development of innovative
academic and applied-learning initiatives that respond to the
evolving needs of the commercial and residential real estate
sectors.

The Department of Finance, Real Estate, and Decision Sciences in
the W. Frank Barton School of Business invites applications for a
nine-month, tenure-track position as Assistant Professor of Real
Estate, beginning August of 2027.

Successful candidates will also play an important role in the
academic leadership and continued development of the Real Estate
program, with the opportunity to assume formal program leadership
responsibilities accompanied by an additional stipend. The
candidate will be actively engaged with the Center for Real Estate
and its research, educational, and industry partnership activities.
As the candidate develops in the role, and depending on
qualifications and mutual interest, there may also be an
opportunity to serve as Director of the Center for Real
Estate.

Wichita State University places applied learning at the center of
student experience. Every degree program at Wichita State includes
a guaranteed applied learning or research experience, providing
students with opportunities to develop relevant professional skills
and meaningful experience before graduation. The successful
candidate will have opportunities to integrate these experiences
into real estate education through industry-engaged projects,
experiential learning, research, and partnerships with the regional
business and real estate community.

The Barton School is housed in Wayne and Kay Woolsey Hall, a
state-of-the-art, 125,000-square-foot facility located on Wichita
State University's Innovation Campus. The Innovation Campus creates
a distinctive environment where students, faculty, and industry
interact in close proximity. Major organizations with a presence on
or adjacent to the Innovation Campus include Airbus, Deloitte's
Smart Factory, NetApp, Spirit AeroSystems, Textron Aviation, and
other industry partners. Wichita State University is classified as
a high research activity institution and provides faculty with
opportunities and institutional support for research,
interdisciplinary collaboration, external funding, and
industry-engaged scholarship.

Job Summary

Teach courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels using
various instructional deliveries (e.g., traditional (face-to-face),
hybrid, and fully online). To foster applied learning into the
course design and engage with industry and local business community
applied projects. To advance knowledge through scholarly activities
(e.g., active involvement in committees, student mentorship,
recruitment and retention initiative, outreach activities,
etc.)

Essential Functions

Meet expectations for research, teaching, and service as set forth
by the department and college.

Job Duties

The successful candidate will be expected to:
1. Teaching : Teach two courses per semester (four courses
per academic year) in the Real Estate program at the undergraduate
and graduate levels, with courses offered in both in-person and
online formats. Teaching assignments may include, depending on the
candidate's expertise and program needs, Principles of Real Estate,
Real Estate Finance, Real Estate Valuation and Appraisal, Real
Estate Law, Property Management, Real Estate Investment Analysis,
Urban Land Development, and other related courses.

2. Applied Learning and Industry Engagement : Incorporate
applied and experiential learning into course design and develop
meaningful opportunities for students to engage with the real
estate industry and broader business community through applied
projects, case studies, professional engagement, and other
experiential learning activities.

3. Research : Develop and maintain an active and sustainable
research program consistent with AACSB Scholarly Academic (SA)
expectations and the requirements for tenure and promotion at the
Barton School of Business. The successful candidate will be
expected to produce high-quality scholarly research with the
potential for publication in respected and leading journals in real
estate, finance, economics, or closely related fields.

4. Service and Engagement : Contribute meaningful service to
the department, Barton School of Business, university, profession,
and broader community. Service may include participation in
committees, student mentoring, student recruitment and retention
initiatives, professional organizations, industry engagement,
outreach activities, and other activities that advance the mission
of the department and school.

Required Education and Experience:

Terminal degree in direct field
Teaching experience

Faculty Requirements

A Ph.D. in Real Estate Finance, Economics or a closely related
field from an accredited institution, with demonstrated teaching
and/or research expertise in real estate.
Applicants who are at an advanced stage of their doctoral
studies (ABD) will be considered if they provide strong evidence
that all degree requirements will be completed by the end of May
2027.


Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Potential to pursue externally funded or industry-supported
research.
Ability and interest in developing productive partnerships with
the real estate and broader business community.
Ability to provide instruction curriculum to a variety of
learners.
Commitment to collaborative processes and environments.
Strong written, interpersonal, and oral communication
skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

Doctoral degree completed or in progress at an AACSB-accredited
institution.
Relevant professional or industry experience in real estate or
a closely related field.
Experience incorporating applied or experiential learning into
teaching.
Research expertise directly related to real estate and its
application to industry, communities, or public policy.

Evidence of an established record of scholarly research or a
strong research pipeline with demonstrated potential for
publication in high-quality real estate, finance, economics, or
related academic journals.
Evidence of, or demonstrated potential for, effective teaching
in real estate or related areas. Evidence may include teaching
evaluations, course development, applied-learning activities,
instructional technologies or software, experience with multiple
instructional delivery formats, or other indicators of teaching
effectiveness.

REQUIRED MATERIALS
1. Cover Letter/Letter of application addressing how the
candidate’s qualifications and experience align with the
position.

2. Teaching Statement: A statement (1-2 pages) describing teaching
approach/philosophy and experience (including course topics the
candidate can teach, mentoring experience, and any evidence of
teaching effectiveness).

3. Research Statement: A statement (1-2 pages) describing research
approach/philosophy and experience.

Physical Requirements:

Ability to remain in a stationary position – Frequent 60-90%;
Ability to operate a computer and other office equipment including
but not limited to phone, printers, copiers, and calculators –
Frequent 60-90%
